papers.title_in_file: Quantum convolutional neural network for classical data classification
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: Benchmark of fully parameterized quantum CNN models for MNIST and Fashion MNIST classification, run in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that QCNN models with 12 to 51 free parameters reached a best case of about 99% on MNIST and about 94% on Fashion MNIST.
quotes: best case being about 99% for MNIST and about 94% for Fashion MNIST.
ranging from 12 to 51
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one benchmark study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the QCNN models performed noticeably better than CNN models under similar training conditions.
quotes: The QCNN models performed noticeably better than CNN models under the similar training conditions.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that verification through real-world experiments and noisy simulations remains to be done, and that testing performance as the QCNN models grow bigger remains future work.
quotes: However, the verification through real-world experiments and noisy simulations remains to be done.
Furthermore, testing the classification performance as the QCNN models grow bigger remains an interesting future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: stated limit

papers.title_in_file: Higher-order topological kernels via quantum computation
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a quantum topological-data-analysis kernel built from Betti curves with the LGZ algorithm, with a noiseless-simulator prototype.

assertions.value: The paper establishes an upper bound on the error of the LGZ-based Betti-number estimate and demonstrates that the resulting topological kernel is a Mercer kernel.
assertions.anchor: Section IV and Conclusion (Proposition on Mercer kernel)
quotes: We have established an upper bound on the error that may arise from the use of this algorithm and demonstrated that the resulting kernel satisfies the criteria of a Mercer kernel.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a proposition with proof in the paper (Section IV, Proposition 2).

assertions.value: The authors report that on a synthetic shape-classification dataset of 100 items, the topological kernel computed classically gave the best performance compared with Gaussian, Laplacian and polynomial kernels and was the only one that improved as more points were sampled.
quotes: The dataset created has 100 items and is balanced.
Notably, the topological kernel yields the best performance compared to the conventional kernels.
More importantly, the topological technique is the only one that exhibits improvement in performance with an increase in sampled points.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single small synthetic benchmark.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors attribute the result to inductive bias for a task that is topological by construction.

assertions.value: The authors report that in noiseless simulation the Trotter technique reached zero RMSE against the exact kernel with only two repetitions, and that 200 shots were sufficient to estimate the coefficients accurately.
quotes: yet yields the best performance (zero RMSE) with only two repetitions.
The number of shots needed is relatively unimportant, as 200 shots are sufficient to accurately estimate the coefficients.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result on a small dataset.

assertions.value: The authors state the prototype was implemented on a noiseless simulator, and that efficient analysis of higher-order Betti numbers is expected on quantum hardware assuming large-scale fault-tolerant hardware is available.
quotes: We exhibit a working prototype of our approach implemented on a noiseless simulator
assuming large-scale fault-tolerant quantum hardware is available
assertions.certainty_reason: scope

papers.title_in_file: H-DES: a Quantum-Classical Hybrid Differential Equation Solver
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: A variational hybrid algorithm for solving differential equations, shown on emulators and one run on IBM hardware; authors are from ColibriTD and the method is patent-pending.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a hybrid quantum-classical variational algorithm that uses a spectral decomposition of trial functions encoded in quantum states and turns solving differential equations into an optimization problem.
quotes: The algorithm relies on a spectral decomposition of the trial functions that are encoded directly in the quantum states generated by different parametrized circuits, and transforms the task of solving the differential equations into an optimization problem.
assertions.certainty_reason: Paper's own definition of its method, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report one run on IBM Quantum backend Brisbane (January 2025) of a first-order ODE with 3 qubits, ansatz depth 2 and 20 SLSQP iterations, with 20000 shots, ending at a final loss of 0.052, and describe it as the first successful resolution of a differential equation on a NISQ device using the H-DES algorithm.
quotes: We run the algorithm using 3 qubits
of depth 2, and 20 iterations of the SLSQP optimizer
using 20000 shots
The execution was made on IBM Quantum backend Brisbane (January 2025)
final loss equal to 0.052
This constitutes the first successful resolution of a differential equation on a NISQ device using the H-DES algorithm.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single hardware run of a simple ODE by the method's authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware test covers one simple equation.

assertions.value: The authors state a belief that the main expected advantage is the potential to return very precise solutions with a limited amount of quantum resources, and describe depth scaling at most linearly with qubit number as a preliminary empirical observation.
quotes: we believe that the main expected advantage provided by the algorithm is its potential to return very precise solutions with a limited amount of quantum resources.
Preliminary empirical observations on various equations seem to indicate that the depth is scaling at most linearly (sometimes logarithmically) with the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim, not demonstrated at scale.

assertions.value: The authors state that the natural next steps are to demonstrate the algorithm on more complicated simulations and models.
quotes: The natural next steps will be to demonstrate the ability of our algorithm to perform on more complicated simulations and models
assertions.certainty_reason: stated limit

papers.title_in_file: CQural: A Novel CNN based Hybrid Architecture for Quantum Continual Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid CNN plus 1-qubit quantum layer for continual learning, tested on MNIST and CIFAR-10 with training curves and GradCAM views.

assertions.value: The authors report that the hybrid architecture showed no catastrophic forgetting during continual learning on MNIST and CIFAR-10, while the classical models showed rises in training loss between epochs.
quotes: And found that hybrid architecture does not show catastrophic forgetting during the continual learning.
The graph for Hybrid architecture does not show multiple evidence of forgetting whereas classical models have been consistent in showing the rise in training loss between multiple epochs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, shown as curves.

assertions.value: The authors state the major limitation is that the work uses a 1-qubit hybrid architecture, and that it is purely based on experiments with theory developed on empirical proofs.
quotes: The major limitation of this research work is that it is based on 1-qubit hybrid architecture.
Another limitation of this work is that it is purely based on experiments and the theory is developed on empirical proofs.
assertions.certainty_reason: stated limit

assertions.value: The authors state the hybrid model takes four to five times more time to learn, and that it has better explainability.
quotes: Hybrid model takes four to five times more time to learn. However, it has better explainability.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author statement listed under shortcomings, without a table in the quoted passage.

papers.title_in_file: Multidimensional Quantum Walks, Recursion, and Quantum Divide & Conquer
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper defining subspace graphs and giving a time-efficient quantum divide and conquer, applied to Savitch's algorithm.

assertions.value: The paper introduces the subspace graph, which formalizes multidimensional quantum walks, and shows how to combine a switching network with arbitrary quantum subroutines to compute a composed function.
quotes: We introduce an object called a subspace graph that formalizes the technique of multidimensional quantum walks.
we show how to combine a switching network with arbitrary quantum subroutines, to compute a composed function.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition and construction in the paper.

assertions.value: The paper gives a time-efficient implementation of quantum Divide & Conquer when sub-problems are combined via a Boolean formula, and uses it to quadratically speed up Savitch's algorithm for directed st-connectivity.
quotes: we give a time-efficient implementation of quantum Divide & Conquer when the sub-problems are combined via a Boolean formula.
We use this to quadratically speed up Savitch's algorithm for directed st-connectivity.
assertions.certainty_reason: Proved in the paper (Theorem 1.1 informal; Theorem 5.3).

assertions.value: The authors state they consider one specific kind of composition of subspace graphs, switch composition, and leave more general types of recursion for future work.
quotes: In this work, we consider one specific kind of composition of subspace graphs called switch composition
but we would like to emphasize the potential for more general types of recursion, which we leave for future work.
assertions.certainty_reason: scope

papers.title_in_file: QSeer: A Quantum-Inspired Graph Neural Network for Parameter Initialization in Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm Circuits
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: A graph neural network that predicts QAOA initial parameters for weighted and unweighted Max-Cut at variable depth, evaluated with a circuit simulator.

assertions.value: The authors report in the abstract that QSeer improves the initial approximation ratio and convergence speed of QAOA circuits across diverse graphs compared with prior physics- and computer-science-driven methods, starting at a 6% improvement in the stated range.
quotes: QSeer improves the initial approximation ratio and convergence speed of QAOA circuits across diverse graphs by 6%
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study, upper range not quoted here.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the weighted Max-Cut testing dataset the conventional GNN had a 15.8% average AR loss and a 23.5% worst-case AR loss relative to the labeled scheme, while QSeer marginally improved the average AR by 0.1%.
quotes: The conventional GNN exhibits a 15.8% average AR loss and a 23.5% worst-case AR loss relative to the labeled scheme
QSeer marginally improves the average AR by 0.1% compared to the labeled scheme
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state QAOA circuits were evaluated with the TensorCircuit simulator, using an unweighted dataset of approximately 800K graphs and a weighted dataset of 34,701 graphs.
quotes: TensorCircuit simulates quantum circuits using tensor network methods
totaling approximately 800K graphs.
consisting of 34,701 weighted graphs
assertions.certainty_reason: setup

papers.title_in_file: Tetris: A Compilation Framework for VQA Applications in Quantum Computing
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: A compiler for variational quantum algorithm circuits that reduces two-qubit gates, compared against Paulihedral and others.

assertions.value: The authors report that Tetris reduced CNOT gate counts by up to 41.3%, circuit depth by up to 37.9% and circuit duration by up to 42.6% for various molecules compared with state-of-the-art approaches.
quotes: Overall, Tetris demonstrates a reduction of up to 41.3% in CNOT gate counts, 37.9% in circuit depth, and 42.6% in circuit duration for various molecules of different sizes and structures compared with the state-of-the-art approaches.
assertions.certainty_reason: Compilation benchmark from the tool's authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that for the Jordan-Wigner encoder, on six real molecule benchmarks on an IBM 65-qubit backend, Tetris had on average a 30.68% improvement in CNOT gate count over Paulihedral.
assertions.anchor: Section on Paulihedral comparison, Table II
quotes: six real molecule benchmarks on IBM 65-qubit backend.
For the Jordan-Wigner encoder, Tetris has on average 30.68% improvement in CNOT gate count
assertions.certainty_reason: Compile-time gate counts for one benchmark set.

assertions.value: The authors state that circuit fidelity was measured on a Qiskit Aer noise simulator, not reported from hardware execution in that analysis.
quotes: We use the Qiskit Aer

papers.title_in_file: Quantum sequential scattering model for quantum state learning
papers.partial_detail: Read abstract, introduction, results/experiment sections and conclusion (selected passages via pdftotext); did not read appendices or proofs in full.
papers.what_it_is: A sequential layered model for learning high-dimensional quantum states that avoids vanishing gradients for states with polynomial Schmidt rank, with theory and simulations.

assertions.value: The authors state that theoretical analysis and numerical experiments provide evidence for QSSM effectiveness in learning physical and algorithmic quantum states, beating conventional approaches in training speed and learning accuracy.
quotes: Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments provide evidence for our model's effectiveness in learning both physical and algorithmic meaningful quantum states and show an out-performance beating the conventional approaches in training speed and learning accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that the gradient variance vanishes exponentially with the number of qubits for randomly initialized global QNNs, while QSSM shows a constant scaling of variance magnitude.
quotes: The variance of the gradient vanishes exponentially with the number of qubits when using the randomly initialized global QNNs.
In contrast, QSSM demonstrates a constant scaling of variance magnitude.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result.

assertions.value: The authors state that increasing entanglement in the target states necessitates a larger scaled model, which could reduce learning performance and efficiency, and that a theoretical performance guarantee for truncated state learning remains to be established.
quotes: Our work has indicated that an increasing entanglement, a property of quantum states, in the target states, necessitates a larger scaled model, which could reduce our model's learning performance and efficiency.

A theoretical performance guarantee and the connection between scattering layer dilation and QSSM state learning information flow should be established for a complete story of truncated state learning.
assertions.certainty_reason: stated limit
